No check that the app is in demo mode, so the destructive reset could be reachable outside a demo.

terms.meaning: Returning a demo case to its original seeded state, removing changes made since.

sections.name: File setup, resetSchema
sections.title: Imports and reset rule
sections.what: Loads the response helper, the input rule library, and both services. Defines a rule that allows only the two demo case ids and no extra fields.
sections.why: Keeps the reset limited to demo cases.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new demo case requires updating this rule.

sections.name: POST
sections.title: Reset handler
sections.what: Checks the request, resets the chosen demo case, ensures seed documents are present, and returns a confirmation.
sections.why: Likely reason: one route resets one demo case so the presenter can restore it quickly.
sections.watch_out: This action deletes saved work on the chosen demo case, so it should not be exposed outside demo use.

summary: Web address that resets one of the two approved demo cases to its original state.
purpose: Lets a presenter restore a demo case before a showing.
why: The code comment says the route resets exactly one seed case and never deletes arbitrary created cases.
how: Checks that the body names one of the two demo case ids, calls the reset in the case service, returns 404 if that case is not available, makes sure seed documents exist, and confirms the reset.
inputs: JSON body with a single caseId field.
outputs: A confirmation with caseId and reset set to true, or 400 INVALID_DEMO_CASE, or 404 DEMO_CASE_NOT_FOUND.
risks: Destructive: it clears review packets and official records for the chosen demo case. Nothing in this file checks that the app is in demo mode, so it would be callable in any deployment that exposes it.
debug: A 400 means the case id is not one of the two demo ids. A 404 means the reset service found no such seed case.
